mentions.name: Native C++ music player
mentions.description: A native C++ desktop music player for playing purchased music, offering deeper library curation than existing players: annotating tracks, custom tags for genres instead of simple enums, advanced tag editing, and bulk transactional/undoable library operations. The UI is built with a thin layer of 2D draw commands that can be ported across backends (CoreGraphics, Direct2D, Pango), with a focus on reliability, UI responsiveness, and resource usage rather than Electron.
mentions.problem: Existing players like Doppler for macOS lack the author's desired ways of curating and interacting with a music library, and Electron GUIs compromise on reliability, responsiveness, and resource usage.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm building a native music player in C++ for playing music I bought. I know there's Doppler for macOS but I want different ways of curating and interacting with my library (annotating tracks, custom tags instead of a simple enum for describing genres, advanced tag editing, bulk and transactional/undoable library operations...)
